name: What happens if my cabinet color looks different in the room?

mainEntity.name: Why do custom cabinet finishes look different under daylight, warm bulbs, and morning versus evening sun?
mainEntity.text: Why do custom cabinet finishes look different under daylight, warm bulbs, and morning versus evening sun?

acceptedAnswer.text: Finish samples often look different in the showroom than they do in the home because lighting and surrounding materials change perception. Natural daylight, warm LEDs, cool LEDs, floor color, countertop tone, and wall paint all influence the final appearance. A white that looks crisp in a sample board may read cream or gray once installed, and a wood stain may appear darker in a low-light room. This is especially important in Los Angeles homes with large windows, mixed daylight, and layered lighting. The safest approach is to review large samples in the room at different times of day and under the exact light bulbs that will be used. If the cabinet maker offers custom color matching, ask for spray-outs or sample doors rather than relying on digital images. Color variation is normal, but it should be controlled and intentional, not surprising.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cabinet color can shift because light temperature, sheen, and surrounding surfaces change how the finish appears. Warm lighting can make whites look creamier, while daylight can reveal blue, gray, or green undertones. Always review samples in the actual room before approving a final finish.
